subject: Operational metrics heatmap — prep for Feb QBR (action items)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, logan.wright@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Acme Analytics <ops@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Operational metrics heatmap — prep for Feb QBR (action items)

Team — attaching the heatmap snapshot I pulled for the month and a simple CSV breakout. This is the deck we will use for the operational slide in Thursday's QBR. High level notes up front: latency trend climbed mid-month (~18% p95 increase) tied to a 3-day cache invalidation event; token unit cost improved 7% after autoscale tweaks but tail latency during short bursts remains a concern; overall uptime met SLO (99.95%) except a 2h window on 2028-02-07.

Ask: please review and reply with the following by EOD tomorrow (Tues):
- One line cause/owner and mitigation for any cell flagged red in the heatmap (latency/cost/uptime/usage)
- Any blockers for proposed mitigations (e.g., infra tickets, testing windows)
- One suggested slide blurb (<=2 sentences) aimed at execs that explains cause + next step

Attachments: 2028-02-operational-heatmap-Feb-dashboard.pdf (heatmap + notes), latency-cost-breakout-2028-02.csv

Context: we'll need to surface a single prioritized action for the ops slide — my current vote is to accelerate the KV cache rewrite canary (log metrics show cache churn correlated with the p95 spikes). If you disagree, say so and provide data.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Inference Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, logan.wright@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational metrics heatmap — prep for Feb QBR (action items)

Kim — quick read. Notes:
- Owner: Serving Runtime (me) for the p95 climbs. Root cause looks like inefficient KV eviction paired with a thundering-cache-refresh pattern after a config rollout on 02/05.
- Mitigation: enable conservative TTL + turn on sticky routing for 48h to stabilize working set (low-risk, 30m ops change). I will open infra ticket and target a 02/15 02:00-03:00 PST maintenance window if no objections.
- Slide blurb candidate: "A transient cache churn following a config rollout drove short-term p95 regressions; we will pin routing and apply conservative KV TTLs to prevent recurrence."

Blockers: need approval for the maintenance window and quick rollback plan from Logan for the sticky routing test.

-Markus

-Logan

Thanks Kim — I pulled three bullets we should call out to execs:
- Cause summary (1 line): "Cache churn after a config rollout caused temporary p95 latency regressions; immediate mitigations in flight."
- Impact: "Customer-facing p95 increased by ~18% for three days; no SLA breaches besides the 2h outage on 02/07 (root cause separate)."
- Ask for execs: approval to go ahead with the 02/15 maintenance window and to fund a small reliability spike budget (+$22k) to shorten rollout testing and extend staging capacity for the next 90 days.

I left the Acme contacts on for visibility given their recent uptick in latency alerts; Polara, please confirm you saw the same traces for the 02/05 config rollout window.

Laura
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational metrics heatmap — prep for Feb QBR (action items)

Appreciate the quick turnaround everyone. Two quick additions:
1) Cost note: the 7% unit cost improvement came from transient autoscale policy change; we need to document the config and bake it into the dedicated policy repo so it survives subsequent rollouts. Assigning to me to follow up — I'll attach the policy diff to the ticket.
2) Usage note: Acme's request volume increased 12% week-over-week during the mid-month spike; we should call that out as a demand-side contributor rather than purely an infra regression.

Final slide blurb (my edit): "Mid-month demand surge plus transient cache churn produced short-lived p95 regressions; immediate stabilizations are scheduled and a small reliability investment is recommended to reduce future test windows."

Action commitments: Markus (sticky routing + ticket), Logan (runbook + staging test), Vivek (policy diff + cost note), Kimberly/Laura (QBR slide + exec ask).

-Vivek
